intro: India is the world's largest democracy: a federal republic where hundreds of millions of people vote in elections that take weeks to complete.

chapters.title: The constitution
text: India's constitution, adopted in 1950, is the longest written national constitution in the world. It guarantees equality before the law, freedom of speech and religion, and bans discrimination by religion, caste, sex or place of birth.
The Supreme Court in New Delhi can strike down laws that break the constitution.

chapters.title: Parliament and prime minister
text: The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, has 543 elected members, chosen by first past the post. The party or alliance with a majority there forms the government, and its leader becomes prime minister. Narendra Modi of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has been prime minister since 2014.

The Rajya Sabha, or Council of States, is mostly elected by state assemblies. The President is head of state, elected by members of parliament and state assemblies, and mostly acts on the government's advice.

facts.label: Elected seats in the Lok Sabha

chapters.title: The biggest election on Earth
text: In the 2024 general election, more than 640 million people voted, the largest number of voters in any election in history. Voting took place in seven stages over six weeks, using electronic voting machines.

The rules say no voter should have to travel more than 2 km to vote, so officials trek to remote mountains, islands and forests; for years a polling station was set up in Gujarat's Gir Forest for a single voter, a temple priest.

chapters.title: States and symbols
text: India has 28 states and 8 union territories, each state with its own elected government that runs police, health and much of education. The capital is New Delhi.

The flag has bands of saffron, white and green, with a navy-blue wheel, the Ashoka Chakra, in the centre. The national anthem, Jana Gana Mana, was written by Rabindranath Tagore, who also wrote Bangladesh's anthem. Independence Day is 15 August and Republic Day 26 January.

chapters.title: India in the world
text: India has nuclear weapons and one of the largest armies in the world. It was a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement, countries that refused to take sides in the Cold War, and is a member of the G20 and BRICS.
It has long-running border disputes with Pakistan, especially over Kashmir, and with China in the Himalayas.

cardGroups.title: How power works

items.title: The President
items.subtitle: Elected by MPs and state legislators for 5 years
items.text: Head of state; acts on the government's advice.

items.title: The Prime Minister
items.subtitle: Leader of the Lok Sabha majority

items.title: The Lok Sabha
items.subtitle: 543 elected members, 5-year terms
items.text: The House of the People; decides who governs.

items.title: The Rajya Sabha
items.subtitle: Mostly chosen by state assemblies
items.text: The Council of States; reviews laws.

items.title: The Supreme Court
items.subtitle: Chief Justice and other judges
items.text: Protects the constitution and can strike down laws.

items.title: States and villages
items.subtitle: 28 states; about 250,000 village councils
items.text: States run police and much more; village councils, called panchayats, handle local matters.

cardGroups.intro: Who chooses whom, and what each part of the system does.

steps.title: How a law is made
steps.intro: Most new laws follow these steps.

items.title: A bill is introduced
items.text: In either house; money bills must start in the Lok Sabha.

items.title: Debate and committee
items.text: Members debate it and a committee may study it closely.

items.title: Both houses pass it
items.text: The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha must agree on the same text.

items.title: Joint sitting
items.text: If they deadlock on an ordinary bill, both houses can meet together to vote.

items.title: The President's assent
items.text: The President signs it, and it becomes an Act.
